q: When did God promise everlasting life to his chosen people?
a: He promised it to them before all the ages of time.

q: Does God lie?
a: No.

q: To whom did God entrust his proclamation at the right time?
a: God entrusted it to the apostle Paul.

q: What position and responsibility does an overseer have in God’s household?
a: He is like God’s household manager.

q: What were the false teachers doing by their teaching?
a: They were upsetting whole households.

q: What did the false teachers want?
a: They wanted shameful profit.

q: How should an elder treat these false teachers who damage the church?
a: He must rebuke them severely so they might be sound in the faith.

q: To what did Paul say they should not pay attention?
a: They should not pay attention to Jewish myths and to commandments of men.

q: In an unbelieving man, what is corrupted?
a: Both his mind and conscience are corrupted.

q: Although the corrupted man professes to know God, how does he deny him?
a: He denies God through his actions.

q: What are some characteristics that older women in the church should have?
a: They should be reverent, sober, not be slanderers, be teachers of what is good.

q: How should Titus present himself as an example of good works?
a: In his teaching, he should be uncorrupted, act with dignity, and deliver a sound message that is above criticism.

q: What will happen to those who oppose Titus if he is a good example?
a: Those who oppose him will be ashamed because they have nothing bad to say about him.

q: How are slaves who are believers to behave?
a: They are to obey their masters, be pleasing, and should not argue.

q: When Christian slaves behave as Paul has instructed, what effect will that have on others?
a: It will bring credit to the teaching about God our Savior.

q: Who can the grace of God save?
a: The grace of God can save everyone.

q: What future event do believers look forward to receiving?
a: Believers look forward to receiving the blessed hope: the appearance of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ.

q: Why did Jesus give himself for us?
a: He gave himself in order to redeem us from lawlessness and to purify for himself a people who are zealous to do good works.

q: What should the believer’s attitude be toward rulers and authorities?
a: The believer should submit to them and obey them, and be ready for every good work.

q: What leads unbelievers astray and enslaves them?
a: Their various passions and pleasures lead them astray and enslave them.

q: Are we saved because of good works which we have done or because of God’s mercy?
a: We are saved only because of God’s mercy.

q: After he justifies us, what does God make us to become?
a: God makes us become his heirs.

q: What should believers be careful to do?
a: Believers should be careful to do the good works.

q: What should believers avoid?
a: Believers should avoid foolish debates, genealogies, strife, and conflict about religious law.

q: Who should we reject after one or two warnings?
a: We should reject a divisive person.

q: What must believers engage themselves in so that they will be fruitful?
a: Believers must learn to engage themselves in doing good works that provide for essential needs.
